subject: Climate & Environment
title: The Value of Biodiversity
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Value of Biodiversity.

hook.text: Nature provides services worth an estimated $125 trillion per year — for free.

buildup.text: Pollination, water filtration, carbon storage, and flood protection all come from ecosystems.

discovery.text: Half of modern medicines trace back to natural compounds found in plants and animals.

twist.text: We have screened less than 1% of known species for useful chemicals. The rest is unexplored.

climax.text: When we lose a species, we may lose the cure for a disease we haven't faced yet.

punchline.text: Every extinct species is a library burned before we read it.

quiz.question: How much are nature's services estimated to be worth annually?

details.summary: Biodiversity underpins ecosystem services worth trillions of dollars annually, including pollination, water purification, flood control, carbon storage, and medicine. Over half the global economy depends directly or indirectly on healthy natural systems.
details.whyItMatters: Putting economic value on biodiversity helps translate ecological loss into terms policymakers and businesses understand, revealing the staggering cost of inaction.
takeaways: Pollinators contribute over 200 billion dollars annually to agriculture
More than half of all medicines originate from natural compounds
Ecosystem services are estimated at 125 to 145 trillion dollars per year

faq.question: Why is biodiversity important for medicine?
faq.answer: Over 50 percent of approved drugs derive from or were inspired by natural compounds. Aspirin came from willow bark, chemotherapy drugs from periwinkle, and many antibiotics from soil fungi. Losing species means losing potential future cures.

faq.question: How much are ecosystem services worth globally?
faq.answer: Estimates by Costanza and colleagues put the value at 125 to 145 trillion dollars per year, more than global GDP. These services include water purification, pollination, flood control, carbon storage, and soil fertility.
